nodes.title: director34: 36 lessons on release 58's code (7 live, 2 staged), 9 Opus judges by hand: all seven live lessons pass every gate line on the judges' counts and main's ruling 1 (by the letter of the rule main gave the judges, four of them fail on one to three script rows); staged c4-ch06-t01 passes, staged c6-ch07-t03 fails on 4 script rows; register 3.5 in all nine for the eighth run

After director34: release 59 (a wrap reply is never graded); every worked step that states a value is said over a board that shows it; a second picture request gets a second picture or the reason, never a bare line; a card may name several wrong answers each with its reason; three walk paths (a give-up at a bridge, try-first and "haan", four hearings of a question); fixed forms; the cold read gains a pass; the prompt is checked by code

The rule main gave the judges ("count each step confirmed without a result board as a contradiction") was wider than the gate's own definition (her words against the board); four judges counted by the gate and left the rows to main, who narrowed the rule after the run in the direction that passes: nine rows in five scripts, four live lessons' pass resting on the ruling

The judges' prompt quoted a script sentence that is not in the script, claimed no listed answer holds a cutting word when one does, and left the AI line's question out of its list of allowed endings: written from main's memory of the round, not from the files

Release 58 graded the child's reply to the wrap's question ("thoda mushkil tha") against the closing question and wrote it as a wrong answer: an evidence row per taught skill and a teach-back event in the learner model, on every lesson reaching the two-turn wrap; the offline walk read 0 because its reader calls no model; found by the automatic check on the paid run minutes after it ended, fixed in release 59

With the own reason kept to its named wrong answer (148 said, none after another answer), what holds listening at 3.5 is the child whose wrong answer the script did not name: five judges heard help about a different mistake (a miscount re-taught right angles; twelfths re-taught halves; 1/6 answered with 1/7)

Register has been 3.5 in every topic for eight judged runs while every other axis moved; its largest cause in seven of nine reports is the length and shape of a turn (a first teaching turn of 67 to 74 words to a child who said "pata nahi"; a close and a card at 73), then fixed forms; fixing sentences has not moved it

Answering a second picture request with the no-other-drawing line and "Ab tum batao." where the hint owns a board that is not up: true to the screen, and heard by three judges as refusing a stuck child (8 of the 12 no-picture turns)

Taking the offline walk's 0 as proof that a change to how an answer is read was safe: the offline reader calls no model and read every unmatched line as no evidence, so the path that only a model exercises went to production broken

md.measurements: - `ms-r8-director34` (2026-11-24): 36 lessons (the seven live scripts, `c4-maths-ch01-t02` among them since release 58, and two staged, `c4-maths-ch06-t01` and `c6-maths-ch07-t03`; × steady, stuck, offtopic, steering), Director only, reactive rule-based child typing Latin Hinglish, on int/r6 integration 92 (`a71fde496`, release 58's code), one invocation, 2,798 model calls, about $2.08. Live predicate check exit 1 on nine rows, one at the end of each steady lesson (`readerAgrees`: the wrap reply recorded as a wrong answer); every other gated predicate 0; no safety turn. Nine Opus judges at high effort, one per topic, four lessons each by hand, against a prompt whose rules and clauses 45 to 53 and 16 were fixed before the build finished. By hand: 0 misgrades in 934 keyed answers; 0 false keys; words against the board 0 in eight topics and 4 in the staged c6-ch07-t03 (one worked close over a 12-part bar, in all four lessons); unsaid boards (strict) 0 in all nine. Nine further rows in five scripts state a value over a board that shows the working and not the value (c6 2, c5-t01 1, c5-t03 3, c4-ch01-t02 1, c4-ch06-t01 2): counted 0 by each judge and by main's ruling 1, contradictions by the letter of the prompt's J3. Axes (floor 3.5): listening 4 in c4, c5-t03 and c6, 3.5 in six; worked example 3.5 to 4; class level 4; screen and speech 3.5 to 4.5, up in six topics and down in none; register 3.5 in all nine; promises 3.5 to 4. Pass: all seven live; staged c4-ch06-t01 (stays staged until a second run). Fail: staged c6-ch07-t03. 148 own reasons said, each after its named wrong answer; 12 no-picture turns, no board change inside any. Full table: `docs/design/round7/judgements/director34-2026-11-24.md`. Not measured: real children; speech as heard.
md.decisions: - `dc-r8-director34` (2026-11-24, main, supersedes `dc-r8-director33`): twelve items in `docs/design/round7/judgements/director34-2026-11-24.md`, each with its own reversal. In short: (1) release 59, a reply to the wrap's question is never graded; (2) this run counts as the first of the two clause 43 asks for, under ruling 1, and nothing leaves hold on it: it stops counting if the next run's judges count the ruled-out rows with their result boards still missing; (3) every worked step that states a value is said over a board that shows it, and the checker requires it of confirmations, told lines, the worked close and the child's own step; (4) a second picture request draws the unsaid hint's board as the picture, or says the line with the hint or the key, never the line and an invitation alone (clause 45 fired): reverses if two judges count the hint's board as settling its card; (5) a card may name more than one wrong answer, each with its own reason (clause 46 fired): reverses if a card needs more than three; (6) a give-up at a check-in between skills gets help; a try-first turn and a bare "haan" count at the question; a question is heard at most four times before its answer: reverses if two judges find answers given to children about to get there; (7) "Suno," leaves the verdict, side-topic replies are written per kind of thing said, first teaching turns are 60 words or fewer: if register does not move in two runs the next round rebuilds how a turn is put together; (8) script rows; (9) the cold read gains a fifth pass (each remediation and reason against the wrong answer that routes to it) and reads joints; (10) record labels; (11) the judges' prompt is checked by code against the scripts before a run; (12) director35 is the second of the two runs. **The whole reverses** as director33's: a third run in which a passing lesson fails on something the round's own build introduced.
md.rejected:
- `rj-r8-no-picture-line-and-invitation-alone` (2026-11-24): **tried** (`dc-r8-director33` item 2 as built: the no-other-drawing line, the board kept, help only where it owns no board or its board is up, then the question by the cap) which on a third turn at a question leaves the line and "Ab tum batao." and nothing else. **What broke:** 8 of 12 such turns in director34 gave the child nothing; three judges heard a refusal of a stuck child (c5-t01, c4-ch01-t02, c6-ch07-t01) and a fourth a mild one. The screen rule held (no board change in any of the 12). Replaced by `dc-r8-director34` item 4.
- `rj-r8-offline-zero-as-proof-of-a-reader-change` (2026-11-24): **tried** accepting "the dry matrix reads 0" as the proof for to-brain 052 B2, which changed which reader grades the closing question. **What broke:** the offline reader calls no model and turned every line it could not match into no evidence; with the model, the wrap's reply was graded `incorrect` against the closing question and written as evidence in production (release 58). A change to how an answer is read is tested with a stubbed reader that disagrees; the offline reader now returns what the model's parser returns for an empty label.
